observations.item: Project advisory pages (GitHub) for libexpat, zlib, lz4, zstd
observations.finding: Each page reported no published security advisories at fetch time (2026-10-06).

The official OpenSSL 3.6 release-notes page describes 3.6.5 (2026-09-29) as a security patch release whose most severe fixed CVE is High, published after the v0.1.0-rc.1 review (2026-09-14). The pinned vcpkg baseline resolves OpenSSL 3.6.4. The fetched vulnerability list was summarized inconsistently by the fetch tool (it disagreed on which 3.6.5 CVE is High and on which releases are affected), so the CVE-to-version mapping must be re-read manually from the official page before any disposition is recorded.
observations.apiScope: mmxisf uses only libcrypto message-digest primitives (EVP_Digest*, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA3-256/512) for checksum verification and generation; the listed 3.6.4/3.6.5 issue titles concern DTLS/QUIC/CMP/CRL/OCSP/SM2/EC/CMS paths that are not called. This is a scope reading of titles, not a verified disposition.
observations.ownerDecisionNeeded: Whether to accept OpenSSL 3.6.4 for this candidate with a dated API-scoped disposition, or to move the vcpkg baseline/override to 3.6.5, which changes vcpkg.json and requires a new candidate (rc.3) and a full rerun.

limitations: Preliminary: Windows/MSVC binary SBOMs do not exist for this candidate and the review must be completed immediately before publication.
A project page showing no published advisory does not prove that no unpublished or newly disclosed vulnerability exists.
